source_caption:
War Machine (2017) is a war comedy-drama following General Glen McMahon, a highly confident military commander sent to Afghanistan with the mission of bringing the conflict to an end. Believing he can succeed where others have failed, McMahon arrives with an ambitious plan and a strong sense of purpose.
As he begins working with soldiers, politicians, diplomats, and Afghan officials, McMahon quickly discovers that winning a war is far more complicated than creating a strategy on paper. Political pressure, conflicting interests, bureaucracy, and the realities on the ground begin working against his plans.
The film explores themes of leadership, ambition, military strategy, politics, bureaucracy, and the disconnect between expectations and reality. McMahon's determination becomes increasingly difficult to maintain as the situation around him grows more complicated.
What makes War Machine compelling is its satirical look at the machinery surrounding modern warfare. The film shows how decisions made by powerful people can become disconnected from the realities faced by those carrying them out.
More than just a war movie, War Machine examines the complicated relationship between military ambition, political pressure, and the unpredictable reality of conflict.
💬 What happens when a perfect strategy meets the reality of war?

source_details.synopsis: War Machine is a 2017 American satirical war comedy film written and directed by David Michôd and starring Brad Pitt, Anthony Michael Hall, Anthony Hayes, Topher Grace, Will Poulter, Tilda Swinton, and Ben Kingsley. Based on the nonfiction book The Operators: The Wild and Terrifying Inside Story of America's War in Afghanistan by Michael Hastings, it is a fictionalized version of the events in the book based on United States Army General Stanley McChrystal. The film was released on Netflix on May 26, 2017.
